reply.text:
Yes, usually, and it depends on what kind of tired. Feeling flat from a long day or a rough night is normal to train through, and a lighter session often wakes you up once you're warm. Drop the load or cut a set or two, and keep the movements crisp.

If you're run down for several days in a row, your lifts are sliding, or sleep has been poor for a week, that's a sign to back off. A shorter, easier session or a rest day does more for you than grinding through a bad one.

A good test is to warm up for 10 minutes. If you still feel dead after that, call it a light day. If you want, I can set up a lighter session for today.
